title: M11: Self-guided lesson player and Course 1 (the tool is the tutor)
description: Intent: As a total beginner, I want a tool that teaches me how a computer works from machine code up, with animated diagrams, a coach that guides and helps when I am stuck, and very easy early sessions, so that I can learn alone and gain confidence. Design: docs/course-1-design.md. Includes: instruction cards over the real RV32IM words (describe(word)), a lesson step library and authoring CLI, a scrubbable timeline and live animated machine diagrams, a scene engine and coach (spotlight, predictions, wrong-answer replies, hint ladder, Show me), drag-and-drop card builder, bit lamps, pixel display, progress and mastery, course path, Gallery and Deck, then the 13 Course 1 lessons. Excludes: later courses. Sequencing: build the smallest vertical slice (lesson 1 alone) and pilot lessons 1 to 4 with the student before authoring the rest. DoD: the student completes Course 1 alone; every lesson's reference solution passes its Gherkin checks in CI.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-06): build all of M11 before piloting (no pilot gate); the UI overhaul (M10) comes first. Wave 1 (pure libraries that do not touch web/: E1 describe, E4 timeline, E2 step library, E3 lesson loader and CLI, E12 progress core) starts now in parallel with M10. Wave 2 (diagram kit, scene engine and coach UI, cards, builder, lamps, pixel display, help, path/Gallery/Deck) starts after M10 merges. Wave 3: author the 13 Course 1 lessons with reference solutions and ghosts. The pilot task stays on the board as an optional check.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Maintainer insight (2026-10-06): the student is in Algebra 2 and knows functions as the heart of math; the curriculum should show functions are the heart of programming. Recorded in docs/course-1-design.md as the functions throughline: boxes as variables, cards as operations, function tables lead to loops, composition as chained custom cards, the pixel screen as a coordinate grid (Graph Machine boss replaces Picture Machine), piecewise as branches, domain as undefined/overflow, sequences as loops and recursion, binary as a polynomial, and the machine itself as a one-step state function. Counting by hand was replaced by Multiply, Make your own card, Use it again.

right_now_summary: The UI overhaul leads while teams build M11’s core lesson, timeline, progress, and authoring tools.
